pages.title: One pool, two force models
pages.body: The fountain and the former Particle Storm now share 2,400 reusable bodies and one InstancedMesh. Use Storm mode to add tangential vortex acceleration to gravity and drag. Click the canvas to relocate the source within the pedestal.

pages.title: Force and integration
pages.body: body(), gravityForce(), dragForce(), vortexField(), and integrate() come from the physics core. Each fixed step accumulates forces before symplectic Euler integration. The vortex is an artistic force, not a fluid simulation. fixedStep() bounds catch-up after the tab has been inactive.

pages.title: Age and reuse
pages.body: Expired particles reset their existing body state instead of allocating new meshes. Pre-roll creates a populated first frame. Age divided by lifetime controls ember color and scale. The rendering buffer and simulation pool have fixed capacities.

pages.title: Related lesson
pages.body: Force Field Playground remains the separate ParticleWorld/emitter-wrapper example. It focuses on multiple user-placed field regions rather than a fixed body pool. Both use the shared Artlab context.
